html:
Kampala, the capital and largest city of Uganda, grew around the royal capital of Buganda at Mengo and the fort that Frederick Lugard of the British East Africa Company built on a nearby hill in 1890.

The kabakas had long moved their capital among the hills here. Missions built cathedrals on Namirembe and Rubaga hills, and Makerere college opened on another. The British ran the protectorate from Entebbe, but Kampala became the business centre.

At independence in 1962 it became the capital. It suffered under Amin and in the wars that followed, and has grown fast since the 1990s. The city's hills still carry the shrines of Buganda, including the Kasubi Tombs.
sum: Kampala, the capital and largest city of Uganda, grew around the royal capital of Buganda at Mengo and the fort that Frederick Lugard of the British East Africa Company built on a nearby hill in 1890.
